subject: Free Cash and Stabilization Fund Usage
overview: Councilor Anna Callahan presented an explanation of municipal finance principles, specifically addressing why "free cash" reserves are unsuitable for funding the recurring operating budget. She argued that these funds must be reserved for capital projects and emergencies to maintain the city's bond rating and financial stability.

items.title: Presentation on free cash and operating budgets
items.summary: Councilor Anna Callahan explained that free cash should be treated like household savings for one-time or emergency expenses rather than as income for the recurring operating budget.

items.title: State recommendations and bond ratings
items.summary: Callahan defined free cash as unspent budgeted funds and noted that the state recommends keeping 3% to 5% of the budget in reserve to protect the city's bond rating.

items.title: Stabilization funds and capital needs
items.summary: The presentation highlighted the creation of new stabilization funds and identified over $146 million in combined road debt and capital improvement needs.

items.title: Budget shortfalls and override recommendations
items.summary: Callahan concluded that new growth cannot bridge current budget gaps, stating that overrides and debt exclusions are necessary to cover rising costs for schools and insurance.
